messages.subject: other CDFs
parts:
Hi.

I'm just wondering how to get a CDF for the new affy 'Human Gene 1.0
ST' chip. I've looked on their website but don't see one. Maybe I
need to make one like Ken did for the Exon 1.0 array (I see a 'mps'
file in the downloads area for the HuGe chip). If thats the case, can
someone give me some direction on making a CDF.

Also, if I wanted to analyze U133 from within aroma.affymetrix, then
how would I get a CDF for that ... or what package do I use to make
one from the Bioconductor packages. I could, of course, process this
with the normal packages.

Thanks,
Mark

On 4/27/07, Mark Robinson <mark.rob...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi.
>
> I'm just wondering how to get a CDF for the new affy 'Human Gene 1.0
> ST' chip. I've looked on their website but don't see one. Maybe I
> need to make one like Ken did for the Exon 1.0 array (I see a 'mps'
> file in the downloads area for the HuGe chip). If thats the case, can
> someone give me some direction on making a CDF.

CDF files are in so called "Library files", which are zipped archives.
You'll find the under the "Support Materials" page for each of the
chip types/sets on the Affymetrix site.

FYI: I've added the two chip types under Section "Documentation on
chip types" in "Pages" on the group page.

>
> Also, if I wanted to analyze U133 from within aroma.affymetrix, then
> how would I get a CDF for that ... or what package do I use to make
> one from the Bioconductor packages. I could, of course, process this
> with the normal packages.

As above.

Note, the CDFs for the above chip types are all provided as ASCII CDF
files. Since it is *much* faster to work with binary CDFs, make sure
to convert the files to binary CDF files first. Use convertCdf() in
affxparser for this. See ?convertCdf for more help.

Cheers

Henrik
